newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Renault, Belgian unions agree social plan.
newsitem.headline: Renault, Belgian unions agree social plan.

text.p: French car maker Renault and unions at its plant in Vilvoorde, Belgium have reached agreement on a social plan for the closure of the plan, Belgian radio said on Thursday.
The radio said the plan offered workers a combination of unemployment payments, cash premiums and jobs for 400 workers on the Vilvoorde site.
"There will be 400 jobs, but we regret they will not be industrial jobs," union leader Karel Gacoms told Belgian radio.
The radio said the 400 jobs would be mainly in maintenance and other support functions.
Under the plan, workers will not be fired, but classed as "technically unemployed" for two years while they look for another job, helped by an outplacement agency.
Their state-paid unemployment benefits will be complemented by cash payments by Renault, which will guarantee a salary with a maximum of 45,000 francs.

After two years, Renault will pay a 10,000 franc premium per month per worker for a period of between three and five years. On average, workers will get 900,000 francs gross in cash payments. Another 640 workers, aged over 50, will take early retirement.
The social plan will be presented to the plant's 3,100 workers on Friday. They will vote on it next week.
